tldr: Individual Oregonians (residents and small businesses) submitted survey responses on economic competitiveness. Dominant themes: strong support for expanding Preschool for All as workforce investment; divergent views on business regulation (some want deregulation citing Idaho/Florida/Texas models; others want higher corporate/wealth taxation); concern about data center tax incentives and environmental impacts; emphasis on education funding, childcare access, workforce training, and affordable housing as keys to prosperity.

bullets.text: Preschool for All cited repeatedly by respondents as critical workforce and economic tool, with claims of 3-to-1 return on investment and raising family incomes by approximately 22% on average.
Data centers mentioned frequently as controversial: respondents question tax breaks, environmental impacts (water/land/energy use), and call for moratorium until transparency requirements met.

Respondents invoke contrasting models: those opposing regulation cite Florida, Texas, Idaho as low-tax/low-regulation examples; those favoring progressive policy cite New York, New Mexico, Nordic countries.
Workforce development emphasized through education investment, union labor advocacy, living wages, apprenticeships, teacher compensation, and childcare access to enable labor force participation.
Tax policy split: some respondents advocate reduced business/personal taxes; others advocate higher taxes on wealthy and corporations to fund education, housing, childcare, and public services.

Housing affordability, zoning reform (ADUs, middle housing, urban density), and property tax system overhaul (overturning Measure 5 and Measure 50) cited as tools to increase housing supply and infrastructure funding.
Environmental transition priorities: clean energy, EV infrastructure, public transit, building codes, restrictions on fossil fuel expansion and data center sprawl on farmland.
